page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the E2 instance family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor, with 2 threads per core and dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the e2-highcpu-4 delivers moderate to weak performance depending on the workload. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests falls into the bottom 25% tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 6104.44. Memory performance is constrained, with a PassMark memory score in the bottom 10%, though uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths achieve average ratings at 46.92 GB/sec and 33.89 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is rated poor.

The instance offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints, leveraging its dedicated AMD EPYC cores. However, the low memory allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU represents a significant tradeoff, making it unsuitable for memory-intensive applications or large databases, as reflected in its weak PassMark database operations and Redis SET benchmarks. This server is best suited for lightweight compute-bound workloads, basic text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, or small-scale web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 compute-focused virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor with 2 physical cores. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place the server primarily in the lower tiers, with weak single-core and multi-core CPU scores, and poor overall memory performance. However, it maintains average throughput for large-block uncached memory transfers and single-threaded compression tasks. Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core, the e2-highcpu-4 represents a resource-dense, cost-efficient option for lightweight compute workloads, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving where memory demands are minimal.
